title: Bringing First-Class SGLang Serving to llm-d
org: llm-d and SGLang (Google, IBM Research and SGLang maintainers)
gist: SGLang now runs inside llm-d's Kubernetes router next to vLLM, with each data-parallel rank exposed so routing can follow its cache. On GLM-5.2 with replayed coding-agent traces on 16 H200s, sessions outgrew GPU memory past 32 concurrent, and by 128 the cache hit rate was 6%. Spilling the cache to host memory kept reuse at 85 to 95%. A third tier on shared storage cost time in steady state and paid off when a pod failed.
changes: Cache capacity is a load-aware setting in its own right. A host-memory tier matters once sessions outgrow GPU memory, here past 32 concurrent, and was then worth almost 4x. The shared-storage tier is insurance that costs first-token time every day and pays only when a pod fails.
caveats: The project's own measurements on one model, one chip and one public trace set. The baseline at 128 sessions, GPU memory only with a 174-second median first token, is a setting nobody would run in production. The storage tier's cost comes from synchronous write-through and prefetch settings; no asynchronous setting is reported.
